src.q: 4.3 Contraindications Hypersensitivity to the active substances or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.

items.t: Any acute metabolic acidosis (e.g. lactic acidosis, diabetic ketoacidosis); diabetic pre-coma.

src.q: Any type of acute metabolic acidosis (such as lactic acidosis, diabetic ketoacidosis) (see section 4.4). Diabetic pre-coma.

items.t: Severe renal failure (eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m²).

src.q: Severe renal failure (eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m2)

items.t: Acute conditions that may alter renal function: dehydration, severe infection, shock.

src.q: Acute conditions with the potential to alter renal function such as: dehydration, severe infection, shock

items.t: Disease that may cause tissue hypoxia: decompensated heart failure, respiratory failure, recent myocardial infarction, shock.

src.q: decompensated heart failure, respiratory failure, recent myocardial infarction, shock

items.t: Hepatic impairment; acute alcohol intoxication, alcoholism.

src.q: Hepatic impairment, acute alcohol intoxication, alcoholism (see sections 4.2 and 4.5).

items.t: Lactic acidosis (metformin; very rare, serious): risk rises with acute worsening of renal function, cardiorespiratory illness or sepsis. Stop metformin temporarily in dehydration. Start antihypertensives, diuretics and NSAIDs with caution.

src.q: In case of dehydration (severe diarrhoea or vomiting, fever or reduced fluid intake), metformin should be temporarily discontinued and contact with a health care professional is recommended.
Medicinal products that can acutely impair renal function (such as antihypertensives, diuretics and NSAIDs) should be initiated with caution in metformin-treated patients.

items.t: Diabetic ketoacidosis (empagliflozin; rare, can be fatal, may occur with glucose below 14 mmol/L): assess at once if symptoms; stop immediately if suspected. Interrupt when hospitalised for major surgery or acute serious illness and monitor ketones. Restarting after DKA on an SGLT2 inhibitor is not recommended unless another clear cause was resolved. Caution in higher-risk patients.

src.q: In patients where DKA is suspected or diagnosed, treatment with empagliflozin should be discontinued immediately.
Treatment should be interrupted in patients who are hospitalised for major surgical procedures or acute serious medical illnesses. Monitoring of ketones is recommended in these patients.
Restarting SGLT2 inhibitor treatment in patients with previous DKA while on SGLT2 inhibitor treatment is not recommended, unless another clear precipitating factor is identified and resolved.

items.t: Heart failure: stable chronic heart failure - may be used with regular monitoring of cardiac and renal function. Acute and unstable heart failure - contraindicated (metformin).

src.q: In patients with stable chronic heart failure, Synjardy may be used with a regular monitoring of cardiac and renal function.
For patients with acute and unstable heart failure, Synjardy is contraindicated due to the metformin component

items.t: Surgery under general, spinal or epidural anaesthesia: stop metformin at the time of surgery; restart no earlier than 48 hours after, once renal function is re-checked and stable. Iodinated contrast: stop before or at imaging; restart at least 48 hours after.

src.q: Metformin must be discontinued at the time of surgery under general, spinal or epidural anaesthesia.

Metformin should be discontinued prior to or at the time of the imaging procedure and not restarted until at least 48 hours after, provided that renal function has been re-evaluated and found to be stable

items.t: Volume depletion: caution in known cardiovascular disease, antihypertensive users with a history of hypotension, and age 75 and over. In illness with fluid loss monitor volume status and electrolytes; consider interrupting until corrected.

src.q: caution should be exercised in patients for whom a empagliflozin-induced drop in blood pressure could pose a risk, such as patients with known cardiovascular disease, patients on anti-hypertensive therapy with a history of hypotension or patients aged 75 years and older
Temporary interruption of treatment with Synjardy should be considered until the fluid loss is corrected.

items.t: Complicated urinary tract infection: consider temporary interruption. Fournier's gangrene: if suspected, stop and treat urgently.

src.q: Temporary interruption of treatment should be considered in patients with complicated urinary tract infections.
If Fournier's gangrene is suspected, Synjardy should be discontinued and prompt treatment (including antibiotics and surgical debridement) should be instituted.

items.t: Mitochondrial disease (MELAS, MIDD): metformin not recommended; withdraw immediately if suggestive signs appear.

src.q: metformin is not recommended due to the risk of lactic acidosis exacerbation and neurologic complications which may lead to worsening of the disease.

items.t: Vitamin B12 may fall: check if deficiency is suspected; consider periodic checks in those at risk.

src.q: In case of suspicion of vitamin B12 deficiency (such as anaemia or neuropathy), vitamin B12 serum levels should be monitored.
Periodic vitamin B12 monitoring could be necessary in patients with risk factors for vitamin B12 deficiency.

items.t: Lower limb amputation seen with another SGLT2 inhibitor: counsel on foot care. Hepatic injury reported (causal link not established). Raised haematocrit: investigate pronounced rises. Urine glucose tests will be positive.

src.q: Like for all diabetic patients it is important to counsel patients on routine preventative foot-care.
Cases of hepatic injury have been reported with empagliflozin in clinical trials.
patients taking Synjardy will test positive for glucose in their urine.

items.t: Thiazide and loop diuretics: may add to the diuretic effect (dehydration, hypotension).

src.q: Empagliflozin may add to the diuretic effect of thiazide and loop diuretics and may increase the risk of dehydration and hypotension

items.t: Insulin and insulin secretagogues (e.g. sulfonylureas): a lower dose of these may be needed.

src.q: a lower dose of insulin or an insulin secretagogue may be required to reduce the risk of hypoglycaemia when used in combination with empagliflozin

items.t: NSAIDs (including COX-2 inhibitors), ACE inhibitors, angiotensin II receptor antagonists and diuretics (especially loop): may impair renal function and raise lactic acidosis risk - close monitoring of renal function is necessary.

src.q: Some medicinal products can adversely affect renal function which may increase the risk of lactic acidosis, e.g. NSAIDs, including selective cyclo-oxygenase (COX) II inhibitors, ACE inhibitors, angiotensin II receptor antagonists and diuretics, especially loop diuretics.
When starting or using such products in combination with metformin, close monitoring of renal function is necessary.

items.t: Glucocorticoids (systemic and local), beta-2 agonists and diuretics raise glucose: inform the patient, monitor glucose more often, adjust dose during and after.

src.q: Glucocorticoids (given by systemic and local routes), beta 2 agonists, and diuretics have intrinsic hyperglycaemic activity.
The patient should be informed and more frequent blood glucose monitoring performed, especially at the beginning of treatment with such medicinal products.

items.t: OCT inhibitors: OCT2 inhibitors (e.g. trimethoprim, cimetidine, dolutegravir, ranolazine) may raise metformin levels; OCT1 inhibitors (e.g. verapamil) may reduce metformin efficacy. Caution, especially in renal impairment; consider metformin dose adjustment.

src.q: Co-administration of metformin with Inhibitors of OCT1 (such as verapamil) may reduce efficacy of metformin.
Inhibitors of OCT2 (such as cimetidine, dolutegravir, ranolazine, trimethoprim, vandetanib, isavuconazole) may decrease the renal elimination of metformin
Caution is therefore advised, especially in patients with renal impairment, when these drugs are co-administered with metformin, as metformin plasma concentration may increase.

items.t: Age 75 and over: special attention to fluid intake with medicines that may cause volume depletion (e.g. diuretics, ACE inhibitors).

src.q: special attention should be given to their volume intake in case of co-administered medicinal products which may lead to volume depletion (e.g. diuretics, ACE inhibitors)

items.t: Alcohol: concomitant use not recommended (lactic acidosis). UGT inducers (e.g. rifampicin, phenytoin): co-treatment not recommended. Lithium levels may fall: monitor more often (these are not in this tool's list).

src.q: Alcohol intoxication is associated with an increased risk of lactic acidosis, particularly in cases of fasting, malnutrition or hepatic impairment.
Co-treatment with known inducers of UGT enzymes is not recommended due to a potential risk of decreased efficacy.
Serum concentration of lithium should be monitored more frequently after empagliflozin initiation and dose changes.

items.t: Check eGFR before starting and at least annually; every 3 to 6 months in the elderly or if renal function may decline. The SmPC table uses eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m²) or CrCl (mL/min). If no suitable fixed-dose strength, use the single medicines.

src.q: A eGFR should be assessed before initiation of treatment with metformin containing products and at least annually thereafter.
If no adequate strength of Synjardy is available, individual monocomponents should be used instead of the fixed dose combination.

items.t: eGFR ≥ 60: metformin max 3000 mg/day (consider reduction as function declines); empagliflozin start 10 mg, may increase to 25 mg.

src.q: ≥ 60 Maximum daily dose is 3 000 mg. Dose reduction may be considered in relation to declining renal function. Initiate with 10 mg.

items.t: eGFR 45 to < 60: metformin max 2000 mg/day, starting dose at most half the maximum; empagliflozin 10 mg (start only in type 2 diabetes with established cardiovascular disease; continue 10 mg if already taking).

src.q: 45 to < 60 Maximum daily dose is 2 000 mg. The starting dose is at most half of the maximum dose. Initiate with 10 mg.b Continue with 10 mg in patients already taking empagliflozin.
b patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and established cardiovascular disease

items.t: eGFR 30 to < 45: metformin max 1000 mg/day, starting dose at most half the maximum; empagliflozin 10 mg (start/continue only in type 2 diabetes with established cardiovascular disease). Glucose-lowering effect of empagliflozin is reduced.

src.q: 30 to < 45 Maximum daily dose is 1 000 mg. The starting dose is at most half of the maximum dose. Initiate with 10 mg.b Continue with 10 mg in patients already taking empagliflozin.b
b patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and established cardiovascular disease

items.t: eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m²: contraindicated.

src.q: Empagliflozin/metformin is contraindicated in patients with eGFR< 30 mL/min/1.73 m2

items.t: Hepatic impairment (any): must not be used.

src.q: This medicinal product must not be used in patients with hepatic impairment

items.t: SmPC: no data with the combination or empagliflozin; animal studies showed effects on postnatal development (empagliflozin). When planning pregnancy and during pregnancy, use insulin instead of this product.

src.q: However, animal studies have shown adverse effects on postnatal development.
When the patient plans to become pregnant, and during pregnancy, it is recommended that diabetes is not treated with this medicinal product, but insulin be used

items.t: BUMPS: metformin (with insulin if needed) is recommended in pregnancy; SGLT2 inhibitors are avoided as a precaution. With an unplanned pregnancy, keep taking it until reviewed promptly.

src.q: Type 2 diabetes during pregnancy should be treated with metformin, as well as insulin if required. Other antidiabetic drugs should not be used.
you should carry on with the drug you are taking until your appointment, as uncontrolled diabetes is risky for you and your baby

items.t: SmPC: should not be used during breastfeeding (empagliflozin in animal milk; no human data for empagliflozin).

src.q: A risk to the newborns/infants cannot be excluded. This medicinal product should not be used during breast feeding.

items.t: SPS: insulin or metformin are preferred in breastfeeding; limited or no information on other antidiabetics (no SPS advice for the empagliflozin component).

src.q: Insulin or metformin are the preferred choices during breastfeeding.
limited or no published information on the use of other antidiabetic (blood-glucose lowering) medicines during breastfeeding.

items.t: No human fertility studies; animal studies show no harmful effect on fertility.

src.q: Animal studies with empagliflozin and metformin do not indicate direct or indirect harmful effects with respect to fertility

items.t: Most common in trials: hypoglycaemia with insulin and/or a sulfonylurea, and gastrointestinal symptoms (nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, loss of appetite), which mostly occur at the start and settle.

src.q: The most commonly reported adverse reactions in clinical trials were hypoglycaemia in combination with insulin and/or sulphonylurea and gastrointestinal symptoms (nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal pain and loss of appetite).
occur most frequently during initiation of therapy and resolve spontaneously in most cases.

items.t: Also listed: genital infections, urinary tract infection, increased urination, volume depletion (very common in heart failure trials), thirst, vitamin B12 decrease, taste disturbance.

src.q: Vaginal moniliasis, vulvovaginitis, balanitis and other genital infection1, 2 Urinary tract infection (including pyelonephritis and urosepsis)1, 2
showed a higher frequency of volume depletion ("very common": 11.4% for empagliflozin versus 9.7% for placebo).

items.t: Lactic acidosis (acidotic breathlessness, abdominal pain, muscle cramps, weakness, low temperature, then coma): stop metformin and seek immediate medical attention.

src.q: Lactic acidosis is characterised by acidotic dyspnea, abdominal pain, muscle cramps, asthenia and hypothermia followed by coma.
In case of suspected symptoms, the patient should stop taking metformin and seek immediate medical attention.

items.t: Diabetic ketoacidosis (may occur with near-normal glucose): stop empagliflozin immediately.

src.q: In patients where DKA is suspected or diagnosed, treatment with empagliflozin should be discontinued immediately.

items.t: Fournier's gangrene: urgent care for genital or perineal pain, tenderness, redness or swelling with fever or malaise.

src.q: Patients should be advised to seek medical attention if they experience a combination of symptoms of pain, tenderness, erythema, or swelling in the genital or perineal area, with fever or malaise.

items.t: eGFR before starting; consider ketoacidosis risk factors.

src.q: Prior to empagliflozin/metformin initiation and periodically during treatment, i.e. at least yearly
Before initiating empagliflozin, factors in the patient history that may predispose to ketoacidosis should be considered.

items.t: Renal function at least yearly (every 3 to 6 months if elderly or at risk of decline) and before starting medicines that may harm the kidneys. Cardiac and renal function regularly in stable chronic heart failure. Vitamin B12 if deficiency suspected or risk factors.

src.q: renal function should be assessed more frequently, e.g. every 3-6 months.
Prior to initiation of any concomitant medicinal product that may have a negative impact on renal function.
In patients with stable chronic heart failure, Synjardy may be used with a regular monitoring of cardiac and renal function.

items.t: Hospital admission for major surgery or acute serious illness: interrupt and monitor blood ketones.

src.q: monitor ketones during this period - measurement of blood ketone levels is preferred to urine

items.t: Children: follow growth and puberty.

src.q: a careful follow-up of the effect of metformin on these parameters in metformin-treated children, especially prepubescent children, is recommended.

items.t: Stop if DKA or lactic acidosis is suspected, or if Fournier's gangrene is suspected. Stop temporarily in dehydration, at surgery and around iodinated contrast.

src.q: In patients where DKA is suspected or diagnosed, treatment with empagliflozin should be discontinued immediately.
In case of suspected symptoms, the patient should stop taking metformin and seek immediate medical attention.

items.t: Twice daily with meals; swallow whole with water. Keep carbohydrate intake spread through the day.

src.q: Synjardy should be taken twice daily with meals to reduce the gastrointestinal adverse reactions associated with metformin. The tablets should be swallowed whole with water.
All patients should continue their diet with an adequate distribution of carbohydrate intake during the day.

items.t: SPS (off-label, adults with swallowing difficulties): tablets can be crushed and mixed with water or given with soft food.

src.q: Empagliflozin with metformin tablets Film-coated but can be crushed and mixed with water or given with soft food.

items.t: Know the signs of lactic acidosis and ketoacidosis; stop and get urgent help if they occur.

src.q: Patients and/or care-givers should be informed of the risk of lactic acidosis.
inform them of the signs and symptoms of diabetic ketoacidosis ( DKA ) - see below - and advise them to seek immediate medical advice if they develop any of these

items.t: If you have severe vomiting, diarrhoea, fever or cannot drink, stop metformin for a while and contact a healthcare professional.

src.q: In case of dehydration (severe diarrhoea or vomiting, fever or reduced fluid intake), metformin should be temporarily discontinued and contact with a health care professional is recommended.

items.t: Look after your feet and keep well hydrated. Seek urgent care for genital or perineal pain or swelling with fever.

src.q: advise patients receiving any sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor about the importance of routine preventive foot care and adequate hydration
advise patients to seek urgent medical attention if they experience severe pain, tenderness, erythema, or swelling in the genital or perineal area, accompanied by fever or malaise

items.t: With a sulfonylurea or insulin, take care to avoid low blood sugar when driving.

src.q: Patients should be advised to take precautions to avoid hypoglycaemia while driving and using machines, in particular when Synjardy is used in combination with a sulphonylurea and/or insulin.

items.t: Major depressive episodes; panic disorder with or without agoraphobia; social anxiety disorder; generalised anxiety disorder; obsessive-compulsive disorder.

src.q: Treatment of major depressive episodes. Treatment of panic disorder with or without agoraphobia. Treatment of social anxiety disorder (social phobia). Treatment of generalised anxiety disorder. Treatment of obsessive-compulsive disorder.

items.t: Not for children and adolescents under 18. Safety of doses above 20 mg daily not shown.

src.q: should not be used in the treatment of children and adolescents under the age of 18 years
Safety of daily doses above 20 mg has not been demonstrated.

items.t: 10 mg once daily; may increase to a maximum of 20 mg daily. Response usually after 2 to 4 weeks; continue at least 6 months after symptoms resolve.

src.q: Major depressive episodes Usual dosage is 10 mg once daily. Depending on individual patient response, the dose may be increased to a maximum of 20 mg daily.
After the symptoms resolve, treatment for at least 6 months is required for consolidation of the response.

items.t: 5 mg daily for the first week, then 10 mg daily; may increase to a maximum of 20 mg daily. Maximum effect after about 3 months.

src.q: An initial dose of 5 mg is recommended for the first week before increasing the dose to 10 mg daily.
Maximum effectiveness is reached after about 3 months.

items.t: 10 mg once daily; may be lowered to 5 mg or raised to a maximum of 20 mg daily. Treat 12 weeks to consolidate response.

src.q: The dose may subsequently, depending on individual patient response, be decreased to 5 mg or increased to a maximum of 20 mg daily.
treatment for 12 weeks is recommended to consolidate response

items.t: Initially 10 mg once daily; may increase to a maximum of 20 mg daily. Re-evaluate benefit and dose regularly.

src.q: Generalised anxiety disorder Initial dosage is 10 mg once daily. Depending on the individual patient response, the dose may be increased to a maximum of 20 mg daily.
Obsessive-compulsive disorder Initial dosage is 10 mg once daily.

items.t: Over 65 years: initially 5 mg once daily, may increase to 10 mg daily. MHRA: maximum 10 mg daily over 65 years and in hepatic impairment.

src.q: Elderly patients (> 65 years of age) Initial dosage is 5 mg once daily. Depending on individual patient response the dose may be increased to 10 mg daily
The maximum dose of both medicines has therefore been restricted in patients older than 65 years.

items.t: Known CYP2C19 poor metabolisers: 5 mg daily for the first 2 weeks, then up to 10 mg daily.

src.q: For patients who are known to be poor metabolisers with respect to CYP2C19, an initial dose of 5 mg daily during the first two weeks of treatment is recommended.

items.t: Stopping: avoid abrupt withdrawal; reduce gradually over at least 1 to 2 weeks (4.2), or over several weeks or months as needed (4.4).

src.q: When stopping treatment with escitalopram the dose should be gradually reduced over a period of at least one to two weeks in order to reduce the risk of discontinuation symptoms
escitalopram should be gradually tapered when discontinuing treatment over a period of several weeks or months, according to the patient's needs

items.t: Should not be used under 18 years (more suicidal behaviour and hostility with antidepressants in trials; long-term safety data lacking). If used on clinical need, monitor carefully for suicidal symptoms.

src.q: should not be used in the treatment of children and adolescents under the age of 18 years
If, based on clinical need, a decision to treat is nevertheless taken, the patient should be carefully monitored for the appearance of suicidal symptoms.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to escitalopram or any excipient.

src.q: Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients, listed in section 6.1.

items.t: Non-selective irreversible MAOIs; reversible MAO-A inhibitors (e.g. moclobemide); linezolid (serotonin syndrome).

src.q: Concomitant treatment with non-selective, irreversible monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAO-inhibitors) is contraindicated due to the risk of serotonin syndrome
The combination of escitalopram with reversible MAO-A inhibitors (e.g. moclobemide) or the reversible non-selective MAO-inhibitor linezolid is contraindicated

items.t: Known QT interval prolongation or congenital long QT syndrome.

src.q: Escitalopram is contraindicated in patients with known QT interval prolongation or congenital long QT syndrome.

items.t: Medicines known to prolong the QT interval (class IA/III antiarrhythmics, antipsychotics, tricyclic antidepressants, some antimicrobials such as moxifloxacin or IV erythromycin, some antihistamines).

src.q: Escitalopram is contraindicated together with medicinal products that are known to prolong the QT interval

items.t: QT prolongation (dose-dependent): torsade de pointes reported mainly in women, hypokalaemia, pre-existing QT prolongation or heart disease. Caution in significant bradycardia, recent acute MI or uncompensated heart failure. Correct hypokalaemia and hypomagnesaemia before starting. Stable cardiac disease: consider ECG review first.

src.q: Caution is advised in patients with significant bradycardia; or in patients with recent acute myocardial infarction or uncompensated heart failure.
Electrolyte disturbances such as hypokalaemia and hypomagnesaemia increase the risk for malignant arrhythmias and should be corrected before treatment with escitalopram is started.
If patients with stable cardiac disease are treated, an ECG review should be considered before treatment is started.

items.t: Seizures: stop if first seizure or more frequent seizures; avoid in unstable epilepsy; monitor controlled epilepsy closely.

src.q: SSRIs should be avoided in patients with unstable epilepsy, and patients with controlled epilepsy should be closely monitored.

items.t: Mania history: caution; stop if manic. Diabetes: glycaemic control may change; adjust antidiabetic doses.

src.q: SSRIs should be used with caution in patients with a history of mania/hypomania.
In patients with diabetes, treatment with an SSRI may alter glycaemic control (hypoglycaemia or hyperglycaemia).

items.t: Hyponatraemia (SIADH), rare: caution in elderly, cirrhosis, or with other drugs that cause hyponatraemia.

src.q: Caution should be exercised in patients at risk, such as the elderly, or patients with cirrhosis, or if used in combination with other medications which may cause hyponatraemia.

items.t: Bleeding: caution with oral anticoagulants, antiplatelet drugs, aspirin, NSAIDs and in bleeding tendency. SSRIs may increase postpartum haemorrhage.

src.q: Caution is advised in patients taking SSRIs, particularly in concomitant use with oral anticoagulants, with medicinal products known to affect platelet function
SSRIs/SNRIs may increase the risk of postpartum haemorrhage

items.t: Suicidal thoughts/behaviour: close supervision early and after dose changes, especially under 25 years.

src.q: Close supervision of patients and in particular those at high risk should accompany drug therapy especially in early treatment and following dose changes.

items.t: Coronary heart disease: caution (limited experience). Angle-closure glaucoma or history of glaucoma: use with caution (mydriasis).

src.q: Due to limited clinical experience, caution is advised in patients with coronary heart disease
Escitalopram should therefore be used with caution in patients with angle-closure glaucoma or history of glaucoma.

items.t: Paradoxical anxiety early in panic disorder (use a low starting dose). Akathisia. ECT: caution. Sexual dysfunction that may persist after stopping. Discontinuation symptoms common.

src.q: A low starting dose is advised to reduce the likelihood of an anxiogenic effect
There have been reports of long-lasting sexual dysfunction where the symptoms have continued despite discontinuation of SSRIs/SNRI.

items.t: Contraindicated: non-selective irreversible MAOIs (start escitalopram 14 days after; stop escitalopram 7 days before), moclobemide, linezolid; all medicines known to prolong QT.

src.q: Escitalopram may be started 14 days after discontinuing treatment with an irreversible MAOI. At least 7 days should elapse after discontinuing escitalopram treatment, before starting a non-selective, irreversible MAOI.
certain antihistamines (e.g. astemizole, hydroxyzine, mizolastine), is contraindicated

items.t: Serotonergic drugs (opioids including tramadol, triptans): serotonin syndrome; caution. Selegiline: caution. Lithium, tryptophan: caution. St John's wort: more adverse reactions (the St John's wort herbal SPC says do not take with SSRIs).

src.q: Co-administration with serotonergic medicinal products (e.g. opioids (including tramadol), and triptans (including sumatriptan) may lead to serotonin syndrome
SSRIs e.g. Citalopram Escitalopram Fluoxetine Fluvoxamine Paroxetine Sertraline

items.t: Oral anticoagulants: careful coagulation monitoring when escitalopram is started or stopped. NSAIDs and antiplatelets: more bleeding.

src.q: Patients receiving oral anticoagulant therapy should receive careful coagulation monitoring when escitalopram is started or stopped
Concomitant use of non-steriodal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) may increase bleeding-tendency

items.t: CYP2C19 inhibitors (omeprazole about 50% rise, esomeprazole, lansoprazole, fluconazole, fluvoxamine, ticlopidine) and cimetidine (about 70% rise): caution; dose reduction may be needed. SPS: watch for QT symptoms when these are started.

src.q: caution should be exercised when used concomitantly with CYP2C19 inhibitors (e.g. omeprazole, esomeprazole, fluconazole, fluvoxamine, lansoprazole, ticlopidine) or cimetidine
A reduction in the dose of escitalopram may be necessary based on monitoring of side-effects during concomitant treatment
Monitor for symptoms of QT interval prolongation in people taking citalopram or escitalopram, who are started on CYP2C19 inhibitors

items.t: Drugs causing hypokalaemia or hypomagnesaemia: caution (arrhythmia). MHRA: monitor magnesium, especially in elderly on diuretics or PPIs. Seizure-threshold-lowering drugs (TCAs, SSRIs, neuroleptics, tramadol, bupropion): caution.

src.q: Caution is warranted for concomitant use of hypokalaemia/hypomagnesaemia inducing medicinal products as these conditions increase the risk of malignant arrhythmias
Monitoring of serum magnesium is advised, particularly in elderly patients, who may be taking diuretics or proton pump inhibitors

items.t: CYP2D6 substrates with narrow therapeutic index (flecainide, propafenone, metoprolol in heart failure, some antidepressants and antipsychotics): caution, dose adjustment may be needed. Alcohol: combination not advisable.

src.q: Caution is recommended when escitalopram is co-administered with medicinal products that are mainly metabolised by this enzyme, and that have a narrow therapeutic index
as with other psychotropic medicinal products, the combination with alcohol is not advisable

items.t: Mild or moderate impairment: no adjustment. Severely reduced renal function (CLCR less than 30 ml/min): caution.

src.q: Dosage adjustment is not necessary in patients with mild or moderate renal impairment. Caution is advised in patients with severely reduced renal function (CLCR less than 30 ml/min.)

items.t: Mild or moderate impairment (Child-Pugh A and B): 5 mg daily for the first 2 weeks, then up to 10 mg daily (MHRA maximum 10 mg). Severe impairment: caution and extra careful dose titration.

src.q: An initial dose of 5 mg daily for the first two weeks of treatment is recommended in patients with mild or moderate hepatic impairment. Depending on individual patient response, the dose may be increased to 10 mg daily.
Caution and extra careful dose titration is advised in patients with severely reduced hepatic function
In patients with mild or moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh Criteria A and B), the half-life of escitalopram was about twice as long

items.t: SmPC: should not be used unless clearly necessary and after careful risk-benefit assessment. Avoid abrupt stopping.

src.q: should not be used during pregnancy unless clearly necessary and only after careful consideration of the risk/benefit
Abrupt discontinuation should be avoided during pregnancy.

items.t: Later pregnancy: observe the neonate (respiratory distress, feeding difficulty, seizures, jitteriness, usually within 24 hours); PPHN about 5 per 1000; postpartum haemorrhage risk under 2-fold after use in the month before birth.

src.q: Neonates should be observed if maternal use of Cipralex continues into the later stages of pregnancy, particularly in the third trimester.
The observed risk was approximately 5 cases per 1000 pregnancies.
Observational data indicate an increased risk (less than 2-fold) of postpartum haemorrhage following SSRI/SNRI exposure within the month prior to birth

items.t: BUMPS: SSRIs are commonly taken in pregnancy without problems; any heart-defect effect is uncertain and small. If well controlled it may be best to stay on escitalopram; do not stop without advice. Hospital delivery usually advised.

src.q: SSRIs are commonly taken during pregnancy without any problem.
If a woman's condition is well-controlled with escitalopram, it may be best to stay on it rather than try something new and risk a relapse.
Women should not stop taking escitalopram without first speaking to their midwife, GP or specialist.

items.t: SmPC: expected to pass into milk; breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment.

src.q: It is expected that escitalopram will be excreted into human milk. Consequently, breast-feeding is not recommended during treatment.

items.t: SPS (differs from SmPC): can be used with caution, but sertraline or paroxetine are preferred. Monitor the infant for irritability, restlessness, drowsiness, vomiting, poor feeding and weight gain.

src.q: Escitalopram can be used with caution during breastfeeding, but sertraline or paroxetine are preferred.
As a precaution, monitor for irritability, restlessness, drowsiness, vomiting, poor feeding and adequate weight-gain.

items.t: Animal data with citalopram: sperm quality may be affected; human SSRI reports show it is reversible. Sexual dysfunction may persist after stopping (MHRA 2026 lists escitalopram).

src.q: Human case reports with some SSRIs have shown that an effect on sperm quality is reversible.
Citalopram, escitalopram, duloxetine, fluvoxamine, fluoxetine, paroxetine, sertraline, venlafaxine, amitriptyline, nortriptyline

items.t: Very common: headache, nausea. Most frequent in the first 1 to 2 weeks, then usually lessen.

src.q: Nervous system disorders Very common Headache
Gastrointestinal disorders Very common Nausea
Adverse reactions are most frequent during the first or second week of treatment and usually decrease in intensity and frequency with continued treatment.

items.t: Common: appetite and weight change; anxiety, restlessness, abnormal dreams, reduced libido; insomnia, somnolence, dizziness, paraesthesia, tremor; diarrhoea, constipation, vomiting, dry mouth; sweating; joint and muscle pain; ejaculation disorder, impotence; fatigue, fever; sinusitis, yawning.

src.q: Common Insomnia, somnolence, dizziness, paraesthesia, tremor
Common Diarrhoea, constipation, vomiting, dry mouth
Common Male: ejaculation disorder, impotence

items.t: Discontinuation symptoms are common (dizziness, sensory disturbance including electric-shock sensations, sleep problems, agitation, nausea).

src.q: Discontinuation of SSRIs/SNRIs (particularly when abrupt) commonly leads to discontinuation symptoms.

items.t: QT prolongation / ventricular arrhythmia including torsade de pointes: if arrhythmia signs (palpitations, syncope, seizures) occur, stop and do an ECG. MHRA: QTc >500 ms withdraw gradually; 480 to 500 ms reconsider or reduce dose.

src.q: If signs of cardiac arrhythmia occur during treatment with escitalopram, the treatment should be withdrawn and an ECG should be performed.
if QTc interval is >500 milliseconds, treatment should be withdrawn gradually

items.t: Serotonin syndrome (agitation, tremor, myoclonus, hyperthermia): stop the SSRI and serotonergic drug immediately and treat.

src.q: If this occurs treatment with the SSRI and the serotonergic medicinal product should be discontinued immediately and symptomatic treatment initiated.

items.t: New or worse suicidal thoughts: seek urgent medical attention (MHRA 2026). GI bleeding (uncommon); hyponatraemia.

src.q: if you have new or worsening suicidal thoughts, particularly when starting or changing dose of antidepressants, seek urgent medical attention
Uncommon Gastrointestinal haemorrhages (including rectal haemorrhage)

items.t: Before starting: correct hypokalaemia/hypomagnesaemia; ECG review in cardiac disease. SPS: ECG, magnesium and potassium before and during treatment if QT risk factors. Discuss suicide risk and sexual dysfunction (MHRA 2026).

src.q: should be corrected before treatment with escitalopram is started
Monitor ECG, magnesium and potassium, before and during treatment with citalopram or escitalopram in people with risk factors.
discuss with patients when starting or changing the dose of an antidepressant or at their next review, the risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviours

items.t: Ongoing: magnesium in elderly on diuretics or PPIs (MHRA); coagulation when starting/stopping with oral anticoagulants; QT symptoms if CYP2C19 inhibitor added; suicidality early and after dose changes.

src.q: Monitoring of serum magnesium is advised, particularly in elderly patients, who may be taking diuretics or proton pump inhibitors
Patients receiving oral anticoagulant therapy should receive careful coagulation monitoring when escitalopram is started or stopped

items.t: Stop if: signs of arrhythmia (do ECG), first seizure or more seizures, manic phase, serotonin syndrome. MHRA: QTc >500 ms withdraw gradually.

src.q: Escitalopram should be discontinued if a patient develops seizures for the first time, or if there is an increase in seizure frequency
SSRIs should be discontinued in any patient entering a manic phase.
if QTc interval is >500 milliseconds, treatment should be withdrawn gradually

items.t: Single daily dose, with or without food.

src.q: is administered as a single daily dose and may be taken with or without food

items.t: Response usually takes 2 to 4 weeks. Do not stop suddenly. Avoid alcohol. Take care with driving until you know how you react.

src.q: Usually 2-4 weeks are necessary to obtain antidepressant response.
Patients should be cautioned about the potential risk of an influence on their ability to drive a car and operate machinery.

items.t: Report palpitations, fainting or fits promptly. Seek urgent help for new or worse suicidal thoughts (NHS 111, crisis team, Samaritans 116 123).

src.q: if cardiovascular symptoms, such as palpitations, vertigo, syncope, or seizures develop during treatment, cardiac evaluation including an ECG should be undertaken
You can call NHS 111, or your local mental health crisis team, Samaritans on 116 123

src.q: is indicated in adults and adolescents 16 years of age and older for the symptomatic relief of osteoarthritis (OA), rheumatoid arthritis (RA), ankylosing spondylitis, and the pain and signs of inflammation associated with acute gouty arthritis
for the short-term treatment of moderate pain associated with dental surgery

items.t: All indications: use the lowest effective daily dose for the shortest possible duration (cardiovascular risk may rise with dose and duration); re-evaluate the need periodically, especially in osteoarthritis.

src.q: the shortest duration possible and the lowest effective daily dose should be used
The patient's need for symptomatic relief and response to therapy should be re-evaluated periodically, especially in patients with osteoarthritis

items.t: Osteoarthritis: 30 mg once daily; may increase to 60 mg once daily if relief is insufficient. Do not exceed 60 mg daily.

src.q: Osteoarthritis The recommended dose is 30 mg once daily.
an increased dose of 60 mg once daily may increase efficacy
The dose for OA should not exceed 60 mg daily.

items.t: Rheumatoid arthritis and ankylosing spondylitis: 60 mg once daily; may increase to 90 mg once daily if relief is insufficient, then down-titrate to 60 mg once stable if appropriate. Do not exceed 90 mg daily.

src.q: Rheumatoid arthritis The recommended dose is 60 mg once daily.
Ankylosing spondylitis The recommended dose is 60 mg once daily.
an increased dose of 90 mg once daily may increase efficacy
Once the patient is clinically stabilised, down-titration to a 60 mg once daily dose may be appropriate.
The dose for RA and ankylosing spondylitis should not exceed 90 mg daily.
the recommended dose is 60 mg once daily

items.t: Acute gouty arthritis: 120 mg once daily, only for the acute symptomatic period; maximum 120 mg daily for up to 8 days.

src.q: Acute gouty arthritis The recommended dose is 120 mg once daily.
The dose for acute gout should not exceed 120 mg daily, limited to a maximum of 8 days treatment.
etoricoxib should be used only for the acute symptomatic period

items.t: Pain after dental surgery: 90 mg once daily, maximum 3 days.

src.q: Postoperative dental surgery pain The recommended dose is 90 mg once daily, limited to a maximum of 3 days.

items.t: Elderly: no dose adjustment, but use with caution.

caution should be exercised in elderly patients

items.t: Hypersensitivity to etoricoxib or any excipient. Bronchospasm, acute rhinitis, nasal polyps, angioedema, urticaria or allergic-type reactions after aspirin or other NSAIDs (including COX-2 inhibitors).

src.q: Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.

Patients who, after taking acetylsalicylic acid or NSAIDs including COX-2 (cyclooxygenase-2) inhibitors, experience bronchospasm, acute rhinitis, nasal polyps, angioneurotic oedema, urticaria, or allergic-type reactions.

Patients with hypertension whose blood pressure is persistently elevated above 140/90 mmHg and has not been adequately controlled.

items.t: GI perforation, ulcers or bleeding (some fatal) can occur. Caution in those most at risk: elderly, other NSAID or aspirin use, history of GI disease such as ulceration and bleeding. Aspirin (even low dose) further increases GI risk.

src.q: Upper gastrointestinal complications [perforations, ulcers or bleedings (PUBs)], some of them resulting in fatal outcome, have occurred in patients treated with etoricoxib.
Caution is advised with treatment of patients most at risk of developing a gastrointestinal complication with NSAIDs
when etoricoxib is taken concomitantly with acetylsalicylic acid (even at low doses)

items.t: Thrombotic risk (especially MI and stroke). Patients with significant cardiovascular risk factors (e.g. hypertension, hyperlipidaemia, diabetes, smoking) only after careful consideration. Not a substitute for aspirin: do not stop antiplatelet therapy.

src.q: the selective COX-2 inhibitor class of drugs may be associated with a risk of thrombotic events (especially myocardial infarction (MI) and stroke)
Patients with significant risk factors for cardiovascular events (e.g. hypertension, hyperlipidaemia, diabetes mellitus, smoking) should only be treated with etoricoxib after careful consideration
antiplatelet therapies should not be discontinued

items.t: Fluid retention, oedema and hypertension; may cause more frequent and severe hypertension than some other NSAIDs, especially at high doses. Control blood pressure before starting; caution with a history of cardiac failure, left ventricular dysfunction, hypertension or pre-existing oedema.

src.q: Etoricoxib may be associated with more frequent and severe hypertension than some other NSAIDs and selective COX-2 inhibitors, particularly at high doses.
hypertension should be controlled before treatment with etoricoxib
Caution should be exercised in patients with a history of cardiac failure, left ventricular dysfunction, or hypertension and in patients with pre-existing oedema from any other reason.

items.t: Renal: may impair renal function when renal perfusion is compromised; greatest risk with significantly impaired renal function, uncompensated heart failure or cirrhosis; consider monitoring renal function. Caution when starting in dehydration; rehydrate first.

src.q: Patients at greatest risk of this response are those with pre-existing significantly impaired renal function, uncompensated heart failure, or cirrhosis.
Monitoring of renal function in such patients should be considered.
Caution should be used when initiating treatment with etoricoxib in patients with dehydration.
It is advisable to rehydrate patients prior to starting therapy with etoricoxib.

items.t: Liver: ALT/AST rises (about 3 times ULN or more) in about 1%. Monitor if liver dysfunction symptoms or abnormal LFTs; stop if hepatic insufficiency or persistently abnormal LFTs (3 times ULN).

src.q: have been reported in approximately 1 % of patients in clinical trials
If signs of hepatic insufficiency occur, or if persistently abnormal liver function tests (three times the upper limit of normal) are detected, etoricoxib should be discontinued.

items.t: Serious skin reactions (exfoliative dermatitis, SJS, TEN) and serious hypersensitivity (anaphylaxis, angioedema), mostly in the first month: stop at the first rash, mucosal lesion or sign of hypersensitivity. May mask fever and inflammation.

src.q: Etoricoxib should be discontinued at the first appearance of skin rash, mucosal lesions, or any other sign of hypersensitivity.
Etoricoxib may mask fever and other signs of inflammation.

items.t: Caution with warfarin or other oral anticoagulants. Not recommended in women attempting to conceive. Lactose: patients with galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take it.

src.q: Caution should be exercised when co-administering etoricoxib with warfarin or other oral anticoagulants
is not recommended in women attempting to conceive
Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take this medicinal product.

items.t: Asthma (SPS): if NSAID-naive or previously tolerant, use with caution and monitor for asthma exacerbation; with a history of NSAID-exacerbated respiratory disease (NERD) do not use.

src.q: Use oral or topical NSAIDs with caution and monitor for symptoms such as exacerbation of asthma.
History of NERD Do not use oral or topical NSAIDs.

items.t: Oral anticoagulants (warfarin): etoricoxib 120 mg raised INR by about 13%; use with caution and monitor INR closely, especially in the first days after starting or changing the dose. Warfarin SmPC: NSAIDs including COX-2 inhibitors should be avoided, or given with caution and increased monitoring.

src.q: patients receiving oral anticoagulants should be closely monitored for their prothrombin time INR, particularly in the first few days when therapy with etoricoxib is initiated or the dose of etoricoxib is changed

NSAIDs (including aspirin and cox-2 specific NSAIDS)

items.t: ACE inhibitors and angiotensin II antagonists (and diuretics): reduced antihypertensive/diuretic effect; further renal deterioration, possibly acute renal failure, in compromised renal function. Use with caution, especially in the elderly; keep hydrated and consider monitoring renal function after starting and periodically.

src.q: NSAIDs may reduce the effect of diuretics and other antihypertensive drugs.

the co-administration of an ACE inhibitor or Angiotensin II antagonist and agents that inhibit cyclo-oxygenase may result in further deterioration of renal function, including possible acute renal failure
Therefore, the combination should be administered with caution, especially in the elderly.
consideration should be given to monitoring of renal function after initiation of concomitant therapy, and periodically thereafter

items.t: Aspirin: can be used with low-dose (cardiovascular prophylaxis) aspirin, but GI ulceration and complications increase. Aspirin above cardiovascular prophylaxis doses, or other NSAIDs: not recommended.

src.q: Etoricoxib can be used concomitantly with acetylsalicylic acid at doses used for cardiovascular prophylaxis (low-dose acetylsalicylic acid).
Concomitant administration of etoricoxib with doses of acetylsalicylic acid above those for cardiovascular prophylaxis or with other NSAIDs is not recommended

items.t: Methotrexate: monitor for methotrexate toxicity (etoricoxib 120 mg raised methotrexate levels in one study). SPS: use NSAIDs with methotrexate with caution on specialist advice; methotrexate SmPC: not recommended with NSAIDs if renal function disorders (even mild) are present.

src.q: Adequate monitoring for methotrexate-related toxicity is recommended when etoricoxib and methotrexate are administered concomitantly.
Taking methotrexate and NSAIDs can increase the risk of methotrexate toxicity.
Use NSAIDs in combination with methotrexate with caution on the advice of the specialist (for example, rheumatologist).
If risk factors such as renal function disorders, including mild renal impairment, are present, combined administration with NSAIDs is not recommended.

items.t: Oral contraceptives: etoricoxib increases ethinylestradiol exposure (37% at 60 mg, 50-60% at 120 mg); consider this when choosing a contraceptive (e.g. venous thromboembolism risk). HRT: raised oestrogen exposure; consider when choosing HRT.

src.q: This increase in EE concentration should be considered when selecting an oral contraceptive for use with etoricoxib.
An increase in EE exposure can increase the incidence of adverse events associated with oral contraceptives (e.g., venous thrombo-embolic events in women at risk).
These increases in estrogenic concentration should be taken into consideration when selecting post-menopausal hormone therapy for use with etoricoxib

items.t: Clopidogrel (clopidogrel SmPC): NSAIDs including COX-2 inhibitors should be co-given with caution. Sertraline (sertraline SmPC): caution with drugs affecting platelet function such as NSAIDs. Spironolactone (spironolactone SmPC): use with NSAIDs may lead to severe hyperkalaemia. Metformin (metformin SmPC): close renal monitoring with NSAIDs including COX-2 inhibitors.

Caution is advised in patients taking SSRIs, particularly in concomitant use with drugs known to affect platelet function
may lead to severe hyperkalaemia

recommend that allopurinol should be offered as first-line treatment for people with gout who have major cardiovascular disease

The therapeutic target is to decrease and maintain serum uric acid below 6 mg/dL (357 µmol/L).

Caution is required when febuxostat is used in patients with alteration of thyroid function
