src.q: Symptoms include acute onset of decreased visual acuity or ocular pain and typically occur within hours to weeks of drug initiation.

items.t: Very rare: agranulocytosis, aplastic or haemolytic anaemia, thrombocytopenia, angioedema, toxic epidermal necrolysis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, pancreatitis, renal failure. Hepatic encephalopathy possible in liver failure.

src.q: Agranulocytosis Very rare Aplastic anaemia Very rare Haemolytic anaemia Very rare
Toxic epidermal necrolysis Very rare Stevens-Johnson Syndrome Very rare
Thrombocytopenia Very rare
Angioedema Very rare
Pancreatitis Very rare
Renal failure Very rare
Possibility of onset of hepatic encephalopathy in case of hepatic insufficiency

items.t: Plasma sodium before starting.

src.q: This must be measured before starting treatment, then at regular intervals subsequently.

items.t: Plasma potassium in the first week of treatment, then regularly (more often in high-risk groups); sodium at regular intervals (more often in elderly and cirrhosis); blood glucose in diabetes.

src.q: The first measurement of plasma potassium should be obtained during the first week following the start of treatment.
regular monitoring is therefore essential, and should be even more frequent in the elderly and cirrhotic patients

items.t: Stop if hepatic encephalopathy, photosensitivity or acute visual symptoms (choroidal effusion/angle-closure glaucoma) occur.

src.q: Administration of the diuretic must be stopped immediately if this occurs.
The primary treatment is to discontinue drug intake as rapidly as possible.

items.t: Swallow whole with water; do not chew. Preferably in the morning.

src.q: to be swallowed whole with water and not chewed.

items.t: Low blood pressure reactions may affect driving, especially at the start or when another antihypertensive is added.

src.q: As a result the ability to drive vehicles or to operate machinery may be impaired.

items.t: Athletes: may give a positive doping test.

src.q: may give a positive reaction in doping tests.

items.t: Diabetes mellitus in adults, adolescents and children aged 1 year and above.

src.q: NovoRapid is indicated for treatment of diabetes mellitus in adults, adolescents and children aged 1 year and above.

items.t: Diabetes mellitus in adults, adolescents and children aged 10 years and above.

src.q: NovoMix 30 is indicated for treatment of diabetes mellitus in adults, adolescents and children aged 10 years and above.

items.t: Prescribe by brand name and device; where a brand has several strengths or devices, also state strength and device (SPS). Any switch between brands or formulations should be under strict supervision; a dose change may be needed.

src.q: NICE guidance recommends insulins are prescribed by brand name.
It is important to ensure patients receive an administration device they have been trained to use.
Where a single insulin brand is available in multiple strengths or delivery devices, using only a brand name is insufficient.
Manufacturers advise any switch between brands or formulation of insulin should be done under strict supervision; a change in dose may be required.

items.t: Transfer to another type or brand of insulin only under strict medical supervision; a dose change may be needed, from the first dose or over weeks to months.

src.q: Transferring a patient to another type or brand of insulin should be done under strict medical supervision.
If an adjustment is needed, it may occur with the first dose or during the first few weeks or months.

items.t: Individual dosing, normally with an intermediate- or long-acting insulin. Usual total requirement 0.5 to 1.0 unit/kg/day; in basal-bolus regimens 50 to 70% may be given as rapid-acting insulin aspart. Give immediately before a meal (onset 10 to 20 minutes, peak 1 to 3 hours, duration 3 to 5 hours), or soon after when necessary.

src.q: NovoRapid dosing is individual and determined in accordance with the needs of the patient. It should normally be used in combination with intermediate-acting or longacting insulin.
The individual insulin requirement in adults and children is usually between 0.5 and 1.0 unit/kg/day.
In a basal-bolus treatment regimen 50-70% of this requirement may be provided by NovoRapid
Due to the faster onset of action, NovoRapid should generally be given immediately before a meal. When necessary NovoRapid can be given soon after a meal.
The duration of action is 3 to 5 hours.

items.t: Type 2 diabetes: start 6 units at breakfast and 6 units at the evening meal, or 12 units once daily with the evening meal; move to twice daily (equal split) on reaching 30 units once daily. Titrate weekly from the lowest pre-meal glucose of the last 3 days (e.g. <4.4 mmol/L: -2 units; 6.2-7.8: +2; 7.9-10: +4; >10: +6); do not increase if hypoglycaemia occurred.

src.q: For patients with type 2 diabetes, the recommended starting dose of NovoMix 30 is 6 units at breakfast and 6 units at dinner (evening meal). NovoMix 30 can also be initiated once daily with 12 units at dinner (evening meal).
When using NovoMix 30 once daily, it is generally recommended to move to twice daily when reaching 30 units by splitting the dose into equal breakfast and dinner doses.
<4.4 mmol/l <80 mg/dl -2 units 4.4-6.1 mmol/l 80-110 mg/dl 0 6.2-7.8 mmol/l 111-140 mg/dl +2 units 7.9-10 mmol/l 141-180 mg/dl +4 units >10 mmol/l >180 mg/dl +6 units
The dose should not be increased if hypoglycaemia occurred within these days. Dose adjustments can be made once a week until target HbA1c is reached.

items.t: Type 1 diabetes: usual requirement 0.5 to 1.0 unit/kg/day, which the premix may fully or partly meet. Give immediately before a meal (soon after when necessary).

src.q: In patients with type 1 diabetes, the individual insulin requirement is usually between 0.5 and 1.0 unit/kg/day. NovoMix 30 may fully or partially meet this requirement.
should generally be given immediately before a meal. When necessary, NovoMix 30 can be given soon after a meal.

items.t: Switching from biphasic human insulin: start with the same dose and regimen, then titrate; monitor glucose closely during and after the switch.

src.q: When transferring a patient from biphasic human insulin to NovoMix 30, start with the same dose and regimen.

items.t: Elderly: intensify glucose monitoring and adjust the dose individually.

src.q: In elderly patients, glucose monitoring should be intensified and the insulin aspart dose adjusted on an individual basis.
there is limited experience with the use of NovoMix 30 in combination with oral antidiabetic medicinal products in patients older than 75 years

items.t: Children and adolescents from 1 year, in preference to soluble human insulin when a rapid onset helps (e.g. timing with meals). Not established below 1 year (no data).

src.q: NovoRapid can be used in children and adolescents aged 1 year and above in preference to soluble human insulin when a rapid onset of action might be beneficial
The safety and efficacy of NovoRapid in children below 1 year of age have not been established. No data are available.

items.t: Adolescents and children from 10 years when premixed insulin is preferred. Limited experience at 6 to 9 years; no data below 6 years.

src.q: NovoMix 30 can be used in adolescents and children aged 10 years and above when premixed insulin is preferred. There is limited clinical experience with NovoMix 30 in children aged 6-9 years (see section 5.1).
No data are available for NovoMix 30 in children below 6 years of age.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to insulin aspart or any excipient.

src.q: Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients (see section 6.1).
Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.

items.t: Must not be injected during hypoglycaemia or suspected hypoglycaemia (section 4.4); after stabilisation consider adjusting the dose.

src.q: In case of hypoglycaemia or if hypoglycaemia is suspected NovoRapid must not be injected.
In case of hypoglycaemia or if hypoglycaemia is suspected, NovoMix must not be injected.

items.t: Biphasic suspension: must not be given intravenously (severe hypoglycaemia); avoid intramuscular use; not for insulin pumps (SmPC section 4.4).

src.q: NovoMix 30 must not be administered intravenously, as it may result in severe hypoglycaemia.

items.t: Inadequate dosing or stopping treatment, especially in type 1 diabetes, can cause hyperglycaemia and potentially lethal diabetic ketoacidosis.

src.q: Inadequate dosing or discontinuation of treatment, especially in type 1 diabetes, may lead to hyperglycaemia and diabetic ketoacidosis.
In type 1 diabetes, untreated hyperglycaemic events eventually lead to diabetic ketoacidosis, which is potentially lethal.

items.t: Hypoglycaemia risk: missed meals or unplanned strenuous exercise. Warning symptoms may change with much improved control, long-standing diabetes or a change of insulin type. With rapid-acting aspart, hypoglycaemia may come earlier after injection than with soluble human insulin.

src.q: Omission of a meal or unplanned, strenuous physical exercise may lead to hypoglycaemia.
Usual warning symptoms may disappear in patients with longstanding diabetes.
if hypoglycaemia occurs, it may occur earlier after an injection when compared with soluble human insulin

items.t: Biphasic suspension may lower glucose more than biphasic human insulin for up to 6 hours after injection; adjust dose or food intake.

src.q: Compared with biphasic human insulin, NovoMix 30 may have a more pronounced glucose lowering effect up to 6 hours after injection.

items.t: Illness (especially infection and fever) usually raises insulin needs; kidney, liver, adrenal, pituitary or thyroid disease can change the dose needed.

src.q: Concomitant illness, especially infections and feverish conditions, usually increases the patient's insulin requirements.
Concomitant diseases in the kidney, liver or affecting the adrenal, pituitary or thyroid gland can require changes in the insulin dose.

items.t: Because it is given with meals, consider the rapid onset in conditions or treatments that delay food absorption.

src.q: the rapid onset of action should be considered in patients with concomitant diseases or treatment where a delayed absorption of food might be expected

items.t: Rotate injection sites (lipodystrophy, cutaneous amyloidosis); a sudden move to an unaffected site has caused hypoglycaemia, so monitor blood glucose after changing site.

src.q: Patients must be instructed to perform continuous rotation of the injection site to reduce the risk of developing lipodystrophy and cutaneous amyloidosis.
A sudden change in the injection site to an unaffected area has been reported to result in hypoglycaemia.

items.t: With pioglitazone: watch for heart failure, weight gain and oedema; stop pioglitazone if cardiac symptoms worsen.

src.q: patients should be observed for signs and symptoms of heart failure, weight gain and oedema. Pioglitazone should be discontinued if any deterioration in cardiac symptoms occurs.

items.t: Check the insulin label before every injection to avoid mix-ups. Seek advice before travel across time zones.

src.q: Patients must be instructed to always check the insulin label before each injection to avoid accidental mix-ups between NovoRapid and other insulin products.
Before travelling between different time zones, the patient should seek the doctor's advice

items.t: May lower the insulin requirement (hypoglycaemia risk): oral antidiabetics, MAOIs, beta-blockers, ACE inhibitors, salicylates, anabolic steroids, sulfonamides; the biphasic SmPC also lists GLP-1 receptor agonists.

src.q: The following substances may reduce the patient's insulin requirements: Oral antidiabetic medicinal products, monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOI), betablockers, angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors, salicylates, anabolic steroids and sulphonamides.
Oral antidiabetic medicinal products, GLP-1 receptor agonists, monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOI), beta-blockers

items.t: May raise the insulin requirement: oral contraceptives, thiazides, glucocorticoids, thyroid hormones, sympathomimetics, growth hormone, danazol.

src.q: The following substances may increase the patient's insulin requirements: Oral contraceptives, thiazides, glucocorticoids, thyroid hormones, sympathomimetics, growth hormone and danazol.

items.t: Beta-blockers may mask hypoglycaemia symptoms. Octreotide/lanreotide may raise or lower requirement. Alcohol may intensify or reduce the effect.

src.q: Beta-blockers may mask the symptoms of hypoglycaemia. Octreotide/lanreotide may either increase or decrease the insulin requirement. Alcohol may intensify or reduce the hypoglycaemic effect of insulin.

items.t: Biphasic suspension in type 2 diabetes: when a GLP-1 receptor agonist is added, reduce the dose by 20% if HbA1c is below 8% (consider a reduction if above 8%), then adjust individually.

src.q: a dose reduction of 20% is recommended for patients with an HbA1c less than 8% when a GLP-1 receptor agonist is added to NovoMix 30, to minimise the risk of hypoglycaemia
For patients with an HbA1c higher than 8% a dose reduction should be considered.

items.t: GLP-1 receptor agonists (MHRA): when one is added to insulin, an insulin dose reduction may be considered to lower hypoglycaemia risk, but reduce insulin stepwise with blood glucose self-monitoring; abrupt reduction or stopping of insulin has led to diabetic ketoacidosis. GLP-1 receptor agonists are not substitutes for insulin.

src.q: blood glucose self-monitoring is necessary when adjusting the dose of insulin, particularly when GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy is initiated and insulin is reduced
Abrupt discontinuation or reduction in insulin doses can lead to poor glycaemic control, with a risk of diabetic ketoacidosis.
GLP-1 receptor agonists are not substitutes for insulin.

items.t: Renal impairment may reduce insulin requirement: intensify glucose monitoring and adjust the dose individually. No eGFR/CrCl thresholds given.

src.q: Renal or hepatic impairment may reduce the patient's insulin requirements. In patients with renal or hepatic impairment, glucose monitoring should be intensified and the insulin aspart dose adjusted on an individual basis.
Renal or hepatic impairment may reduce the patient's insulin requirements.

items.t: Hepatic impairment may reduce insulin requirement: intensify glucose monitoring and adjust the dose individually.

src.q: In patients with renal or hepatic impairment, glucose monitoring should be intensified and the insulin aspart dose adjusted on an individual basis.

items.t: Rapid-acting insulin aspart can be used in pregnancy (two randomised trials showed no adverse effect versus human insulin). Biphasic suspension: limited clinical experience in pregnancy. Intensify glucose control and monitoring before and throughout pregnancy; requirements fall in the first trimester, rise later and fall back quickly after delivery.

src.q: NovoRapid (insulin aspart) can be used in pregnancy.
There is limited clinical experience with NovoMix 30 in pregnancy.
are recommended throughout pregnancy and when contemplating pregnancy
Insulin requirements usually fall in the first trimester and increase subsequently during the second and third trimester

items.t: UKTIS/BUMPS: insulin can be used in pregnancy to treat diabetes; there are no known risks to the baby. Insulin around delivery can cause short-lived low blood glucose in the newborn, which is checked after birth.

src.q: Insulin can be used in pregnancy to treat diabetes.
There are no known risks to your baby from using insulin in pregnancy.
Insulin use around the time of delivery can lead to your baby having low blood sugar for a short period after birth.

items.t: No restrictions during breastfeeding; insulin treatment of the mother presents no risk to the baby, but the dose may need adjusting.

src.q: There are no restrictions on treatment with NovoRapid during breast-feeding. Insulin treatment of the nursing mother presents no risk to the baby. However, the NovoRapid dose may need to be adjusted.
There are no restrictions on treatment with NovoMix 30 during breast-feeding.

items.t: SPS: any insulin can be used during breastfeeding (insulin is a preferred choice); as a precaution, monitor the infant for signs of hypoglycaemia (drowsiness, pallor, sweating or shakiness) and for adequate weight gain.

src.q: Any insulin can be used during breastfeeding, although monitoring is still recommended.
As a precaution, monitor the infant for signs of hypoglycaemia, including drowsiness, appearing pale, or being sweaty or shaky. Monitor for adequate weight gain.

items.t: Animal studies: no difference from human insulin on fertility.

src.q: Animal reproduction studies have not revealed any differences between insulin aspart and human insulin regarding fertility.

items.t: Hypoglycaemia: very common.

src.q: Very common - Hypoglycaemia
Very common - Hypoglycaemia

items.t: Uncommon: urticaria/rash, refraction disorders, diabetic retinopathy, lipodystrophy, injection-site reactions, oedema. Early in treatment, refraction changes, oedema and injection-site reactions are usually transient.

src.q: Uncommon - Urticaria, rash, eruptions
Uncommon - Lipodystrophy*
Uncommon - Injection site reactions Uncommon - Oedema
These reactions are usually of transitory nature.

items.t: Rapid improvement in control may cause acute painful neuropathy (usually reversible) or temporary worsening of diabetic retinopathy.

src.q: Fast improvement in blood glucose control may be associated with acute painful neuropathy, which is usually reversible.
Intensification of insulin therapy with abrupt improvement in glycaemic control may be associated with temporary worsening of diabetic retinopathy

items.t: Severe hypoglycaemia can cause unconsciousness, convulsions, brain damage or death. Mild: oral glucose/sugar. Unconscious: glucagon 0.5 to 1 mg IM/SC by a trained person, or IV glucose by healthcare staff; give IV glucose if no response to glucagon within 10 to 15 minutes; then oral carbohydrate.

src.q: Severe hypoglycaemia may lead to unconsciousness and/or convulsions and may result in temporary or permanent impairment of brain function or even death.
can be treated with glucagon (0.5 to 1 mg) given intramuscularly or subcutaneously by a trained person, or with glucose given intravenously by physicians or other healthcare staff
Glucose must be given intravenously, if the patient does not respond to glucagon within 10 to 15 minutes.

items.t: Anaphylaxis/generalised hypersensitivity (rash, itching, sweating, GI upset, angioedema, breathing difficulty, palpitations, low blood pressure): very rare but potentially life-threatening.

src.q: is very rare but can potentially be life threatening
is very rare but can potentially be life-threatening

items.t: Diabetic ketoacidosis with inadequate dosing or stopping treatment.

src.q: may lead to hyperglycaemia and diabetic ketoacidosis

items.t: Blood glucose monitoring with dose adjustment to reach good control.

src.q: Blood glucose monitoring and insulin dose adjustments are recommended to achieve optimal glycaemic control.
Blood glucose monitoring and insulin dose adjustments are recommended to achieve optimal glycaemic control.

items.t: Close glucose monitoring when switching from another insulin and for the first weeks after.

src.q: Close glucose monitoring is recommended during the transfer and in the initial weeks thereafter

items.t: Biphasic suspension: use pre-meal blood glucose to judge the previous dose.

src.q: Pre-meal blood glucose levels should be used to evaluate the adequacy of the preceding dose.

items.t: MHRA (high-strength, combination and biosimilar insulins): monitor glucose closely after starting a new insulin product and in the following weeks; doses and timing of other insulins and antidiabetic treatment may need adjusting.

src.q: Monitor glucose levels closely after starting a new treatment and in the following weeks.
You may need to adjust doses and timing of concurrent rapid acting or short acting insulin products and other antidiabetic treatments.

items.t: Rapid-acting: subcutaneous injection into abdominal wall, thigh, upper arm, deltoid or gluteal region; rotate sites within a region. A vial is needed for syringe, intravenous (by healthcare staff) or pump use.

src.q: NovoRapid is administered subcutaneously by injection in the abdominal wall, the thigh, the upper arm, the deltoid region or the gluteal region.
If administration by syringe or intravenous injection is necessary, a vial should be used.

items.t: Biphasic: subcutaneous only, in the thigh or abdominal wall (gluteal or deltoid if convenient); give immediately before a meal. Resuspend before use; do not use if not uniformly white and cloudy.

src.q: NovoMix 30 is administered subcutaneously by injection in the thigh or in the abdominal wall. If convenient, the gluteal or deltoid region may be used.
Do not use this medicinal product if you notice that the resuspended liquid is not uniformly white, cloudy and aqueous.

items.t: Storage: unopened in a refrigerator (2 to 8°C), do not freeze. In use or carried as a spare: up to 4 weeks below 30°C; keep the cap on to protect from light.

src.q: Before opening: Store in a refrigerator (2°C - 8°C). Do not freeze.
During use or when carried as a spare: The product must be stored for a maximum of 4 weeks. Store below 30°C.
During use or when carried as a spare: The product can be stored for a maximum of 4 weeks.

items.t: Carry sugar-containing products at all times.

src.q: It is therefore recommended that the diabetic patient always carries sugar-containing products.

items.t: Know hypoglycaemia symptoms: cold sweat, pale cool skin, tiredness, nervousness or tremor, anxiety, confusion, poor concentration, drowsiness, hunger, vision changes, headache, nausea, palpitations.

src.q: They may include cold sweats, cool pale skin, fatigue, nervousness or tremor, anxiousness, unusual tiredness or weakness, confusion, difficulty in concentration, drowsiness, excessive hunger, vision changes, headache, nausea and palpitation.

items.t: Take precautions to avoid hypoglycaemia while driving.

src.q: Patients should be advised to take precautions to avoid hypoglycaemia while driving.

items.t: Check the label before each injection.

src.q: Patients must be instructed to always check the insulin label before each injection

items.t: MHRA: cutaneous amyloidosis can occur at insulin injection sites and affect glycaemic control. Remind patients to rotate sites within the same body region; consider amyloidosis when a patient has lumps at injection sites; advise patients to contact their doctor before moving away from a lumpy area (a sudden change may cause hypoglycaemia) and to monitor blood glucose after a change of site.

src.q: remind patients to rotate injection sites within the same body region to reduce or prevent the risk of cutaneous amyloidosis and other skin reactions
consider cutaneous amyloidosis as a differential diagnosis to lipodystrophy when a patient presents with subcutaneous lumps at an insulin injection site
before changing injection site since a sudden change may result in hypoglycaemia
to monitor carefully blood glucose after a change in injection site

items.t: Diabetes mellitus in adults, adolescents and children from 1 year.

src.q: Treatment of diabetes mellitus in adults, adolescents and children from the age of 1 year.

items.t: Prescribe by brand name and device; where a brand has several strengths or devices, also state strength and device (SPS). Any switch between brands or formulations should be under strict supervision; a dose change may be needed.

src.q: NICE guidance recommends insulins are prescribed by brand name.
It is important to ensure patients receive an administration device they have been trained to use.
Where a single insulin brand is available in multiple strengths or delivery devices, using only a brand name is insufficient.
Manufacturers advise any switch between brands or formulation of insulin should be done under strict supervision; a change in dose may be required.

items.t: Transfer to another type, brand or manufacturer of insulin must be under medical supervision; a dose change may be needed. Two strengths exist: check the label every time.

src.q: Transferring a patient to another type, brand or manufacturer of insulin must be done under medical supervision and may result in the need for a change in dosage.
to avoid accidental mix-ups between the two different strengths of Tresiba as well as other insulin products

items.t: Once daily at any time, preferably the same time each day; when that is not possible, timing is flexible but keep at least 8 hours between injections. Adjust the dose by fasting plasma glucose. 1 unit equals 1 IU human insulin, 1 unit glargine 100 units/mL or 1 unit detemir.

src.q: This medicinal product is a basal insulin for once-daily subcutaneous administration at any time of the day, preferably at the same time every day.
A minimum of 8 hours between injections should always be ensured.
It is recommended to optimise glycaemic control via dose adjustment based on fasting plasma glucose.
One (1) unit of insulin degludec corresponds to 1 international unit of human insulin, 1 unit of insulin glargine (100 units/mL), or 1 unit of insulin detemir.

items.t: Type 2 diabetes: start 10 units once daily, then adjust; can be used alone or with oral antidiabetics, GLP-1 receptor agonists and bolus insulin.

src.q: The recommended daily starting dose is 10 units followed by individual dosage adjustments.
can be administered alone or in any combination with oral antidiabetic medicinal products, GLP-1 receptor agonists and bolus insulin

items.t: Type 1 diabetes: once daily with mealtime short/rapid-acting insulin, then individual adjustment.

src.q: Tresiba is to be used once daily with mealtime insulin and requires subsequent individual dosage adjustments.

items.t: Switching: type 2 diabetes, unit-for-unit from once-daily basal insulin; consider a 20% reduction when coming from twice-daily basal insulin or glargine 300 units/mL. Type 1 diabetes: consider a 20% reduction of the previous basal dose. Monitor glucose closely during and after transfer.

src.q: changing the basal insulin to Tresiba can be done unit-to-unit based on the previous basal insulin dose followed by individual dosage adjustments
transferring to Tresiba from twice-daily basal insulin - transferring to Tresiba from insulin glargine (300 units/mL)
For patients with type 1 diabetes a dose reduction of 20% based on the previous basal insulin dose
Close glucose monitoring is recommended during the transfer and in the following weeks.

items.t: Missed dose: take it when remembered, then return to the usual once-daily schedule.

src.q: Patients who forget a dose are advised to take it upon discovery and then resume their usual once-daily dosing schedule.

items.t: Elderly: intensify glucose monitoring and adjust the dose individually.

src.q: Tresiba can be used in elderly. Glucose monitoring is to be intensified and the insulin dose adjusted on an individual basis

items.t: Can be used from 1 year; no clinical experience below 1 year. No experience with flexible dose timing in children. When switching basal insulin, consider reducing basal and bolus doses to limit hypoglycaemia.

src.q: This medicinal product can be used in adolescents and children from the age of 1 year (see section 5.1).
There is no clinical experience with the use of this medicinal product in children below the age of 1 year.
There is no clinical experience with flexibility in dosing time of Tresiba in children and adolescents.
dose reduction of basal and bolus insulin needs to be considered on an individual basis in order to minimise the risk of hypoglycaemia

items.t: Hypersensitivity to insulin degludec or any excipient.

src.q: Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.

items.t: Must not be given intravenously (severe hypoglycaemia) or intramuscularly (changes absorption), and must not be used in pumps. Never draw it from a pen cartridge into a syringe.

src.q: Tresiba must not be administered intravenously as it may result in severe hypoglycaemia. This medicinal product must not be administered intramuscularly as it may change the absorption. This medicinal product must not be used in insulin infusion pumps.
patients and healthcare professionals should never use a syringe to draw the medicinal product from the cartridge in the pre-filled pen

items.t: Hypoglycaemia: missed meals, unplanned strenuous exercise or too high a dose. Warning symptoms may change or disappear. The long action may delay recovery from hypoglycaemia.

src.q: Omission of a meal or unplanned strenuous physical exercise may lead to hypoglycaemia.
As with other basal insulin products, the prolonged effect of Tresiba may delay recovery from hypoglycaemia.

items.t: Severe hyperglycaemia: give rapid-acting insulin. Inadequate dosing or stopping may cause diabetic ketoacidosis.

src.q: Administration of rapid-acting insulin is recommended in situations with severe hyperglycaemia.
Inadequate dosing and/or discontinuation of treatment in patients requiring insulin may lead to hyperglycaemia and potentially to diabetic ketoacidosis.

items.t: Infection and fever usually raise insulin needs; kidney, liver, adrenal, pituitary or thyroid disease may need dose changes.

src.q: Concomitant illness, especially infections and fever, usually increases the patient's insulin requirement.
Concomitant diseases in the kidney, liver or diseases affecting the adrenal, pituitary or thyroid gland may require changes in the insulin dose.

items.t: Abrupt improvement in control may temporarily worsen diabetic retinopathy.

src.q: Intensification of insulin therapy with abrupt improvement in glycaemic control may be associated with temporary worsening of diabetic retinopathy

items.t: Rotate injection sites; monitor blood glucose after moving to an unaffected site. With pioglitazone: watch for heart failure, weight gain and oedema.

src.q: Patients must be instructed to perform continuous rotation of the injection site to reduce the risk of developing lipodystrophy and cutaneous amyloidosis.
If the combination is used, patients should be observed for signs and symptoms of heart failure, weight gain and oedema.

items.t: Patients must be able to read the dose counter; blind or poorly sighted patients need help from a trained person.

src.q: Patients who are blind or have poor vision must be instructed to always get help/assistance from another person who has good vision and is trained in using the insulin device.

items.t: May lower the insulin requirement (hypoglycaemia): oral antidiabetics, GLP-1 receptor agonists, MAOIs, beta-blockers, ACE inhibitors, salicylates, anabolic steroids, sulfonamides.

src.q: Oral antidiabetic medicinal products, GLP-1 receptor agonists, monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOI), beta-blockers, angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors, salicylates, anabolic steroids and sulfonamides.

items.t: May raise the insulin requirement: oral contraceptives, thiazides, glucocorticoids, thyroid hormones, sympathomimetics, growth hormone, danazol.

src.q: Oral contraceptives, thiazides, glucocorticoids, thyroid hormones, sympathomimetics, growth hormone and danazol.

items.t: Beta-blockers may mask hypoglycaemia symptoms. Octreotide/lanreotide may raise or lower requirement. Alcohol may intensify or reduce the effect.

src.q: Safety in pregnancy has not been established for isosorbide dinitrate.
should only be used in pregnancy and during lactation if, in the opinion of the physician, the possible benefits of treatment outweigh the hazards

items.t: Nitrates pass into breast milk and may cause methaemoglobinaemia in the infant. Use only if benefits outweigh hazards; caution in nursing women. No SPS breastfeeding page for nitrates was found.

src.q: There is data that nitrates are excreted in breast milk and may cause methemoglobinemia in infants.
caution should be exercised when administered to nursing women

items.t: No data on effects on fertility.

src.q: No data on effects of fertility are available.

items.t: Very common: headache (lessens with continued use). Common: hypotension; at the start or after a dose increase, light-headedness on standing, dizziness, drowsiness, reflex tachycardia and weakness. Headache, dizziness, fatigue, palpitations, orthostatic hypotension and flushing may occur at the start and usually settle with a lower dose.

src.q: Very common: headache. The incidence of headache diminishes gradually with time and continued use.
Vascular disorders Common: hypotension.
These symptoms may be associated with dizziness, drowsiness, reflex tachycardia, and a feeling of weakness.
Headache, dizziness, fatigue, palpitations, orthostatic hypotension, and flushing may occur at the beginning of treatment.

items.t: Collapse (sometimes with bradyarrhythmia and syncope); severe hypotension may worsen angina.

src.q: Collapse may occur (sometimes accompanied by bradyarrhythmia and syncope). Severe hypotension may lead to enhanced angina symptoms.

items.t: Very rare: Stevens-Johnson syndrome, angioedema. Frequency not known: exfoliative dermatitis. Uncommon: allergic skin reaction, sometimes severe.

src.q: Very rare: Stevens-Johnson syndrome, angioedema
Uncommon: allergic skin reaction (e.g. rash) which may sometimes be severe.

items.t: Temporary hypoxaemia may occur; in coronary artery disease this may lead to myocardial hypoxia.

src.q: Particularly in patients with coronary artery disease this may lead to a myocardial hypoxia.

monitoring.note: No laboratory or routine monitoring stated in the UK SmPC used (emc 10 mg tablets); no SPS monitoring page found for nitrates.

items.t: For oral administration.

src.q: Method of administration For oral administration.

items.t: Never take sildenafil, tadalafil or vardenafil (erectile dysfunction medicines) with this medicine.

src.q: Concurrent use is contraindicated

items.t: Headache, tiredness and dizziness may occur; do not drive or use machines if affected. Alcohol may increase the fall in blood pressure.

src.q: Headache, tiredness and dizziness may occur. Patients are advised not to drive or operate machinery if so affected.
and/or alcohol may potentiate the hypotensive effect of the tablets

items.t: Prophylaxis of angina pectoris. Not for relief of an acute angina attack (use sublingual GTN).

src.q: Isosorbide Mononitrate Tablets is indicated for the prophylaxis of angina pectoris.
Imdur is not indicated for relief of acute angina attacks

restrictions.note: No prescribing restriction or brand-specific prescribing statement found in the SmPCs used; no MHRA or SPS brand-prescribing advice found.

items.t: Immediate-release: one tablet two or three times a day, taken asymmetrically to allow a nitrate-low period. Nitrate-naive: start 20 mg twice daily. Usual maintenance 20-120 mg daily; use the lowest effective dose.

src.q: One tablet to be taken asymmetrically (to allow a nitrate low period) two or three times a day.
it is recommended that the initial dose be one tablet of Isosorbide Mononitrate Tablets 20 mg twice a day.
The maintenance dose in individual patients is usually between 20- 120 mg daily.

items.t: MR tablets: 60 mg once daily in the morning; may increase to 120 mg (two tablets) once daily in the morning. To reduce headache, may start with 30 mg (half a tablet) for the first 2-4 days.

src.q: Imdur 60mg (one tablet) once daily given in the morning. The dose may be increased to 120mg (two tablets) daily, both to be taken once daily in the morning.
The dose can be titrated to minimise the possibility of headache, by initiating treatment with 30mg (half a tablet) for the first 2-4 days.

items.t: MR capsules: one or two capsules daily in the morning; use the lowest effective dose. If effect wanes on prolonged-release treatment, intermittent therapy may be more suitable.

src.q: One capsule to be taken daily, or two capsules daily, in the morning.
Attenuation of effect has occurred in some patients being treated with prolonged release preparations. In such patients intermittent therapy may be more appropriate

items.t: Do not stop suddenly; taper dose and frequency gradually.

src.q: Treatment with Isosorbide Mononitrate Tablets, as with any other nitrates, should not be stopped suddenly. Both the dosage and frequency should be tapered gradually
Treatment with Elantan LA, as with any other nitrate, should not be stopped suddenly.

items.t: Elderly: no routine adjustment, but special care if prone to hypotension or with marked hepatic or renal insufficiency.

src.q: No evidence of a need for routine dosage adjustment in older people has been found, but special care may be needed in those with increased susceptibility to hypotension or marked hepatic or renal insufficiency.

items.t: Safety and efficacy in children not established (all three SmPCs).

src.q: The safety and efficacy of Isosorbide Mononitrate Tablets 20 mg has yet to be established in children.
The safety and efficacy of Imdur in children has not yet been established.
The safety and efficacy of Elantan LA has yet to be established in children.

items.t: With PDE5 inhibitors (e.g. sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil) - all formulations.

src.q: their co-administration with nitrates or nitric oxide donors is therefore contraindicated
Patients treated with Imdur must not be given Phosphodiesterase Type 5 Inhibitors (e.g. sildenafil).

items.t: Hypersensitivity to isosorbide mononitrate (immediate-release tablets and MR capsules: also other nitrates; immediate-release tablets: also isosorbide dinitrate).

src.q: This product should not be given to patients with a known hypersensitivity to isosorbide dinitrate or mononitrate, to other nitrates or to any of the excipients.
Hypersensitivity to the active substance, other nitrates or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.

items.t: Immediate-release tablets and MR capsules: acute MI with low filling pressures; acute circulatory failure (shock, vascular collapse); very low blood pressure; HOCM; constrictive pericarditis; cardiac tamponade; low filling pressures; aortic/mitral stenosis; raised intracranial pressure (e.g. head trauma, cerebral haemorrhage); severe anaemia; closed-angle glaucoma; severe hypotension; hypovolaemia; toxic pulmonary oedema (immediate-release); riociguat.

src.q: 4.3 Contraindications Isosorbide Mononitrate Tablets 20 mg should not be used in cases of acute myocardial infarction with low filling pressures, acute circulatory failure (shock, vascular collapse), or very low blood pressure
aortic/mitral valve stenosis and diseases associated with a raised intra-cranial pressure e.g. following a head trauma and including cerebral haemorrhage.
Elantan LA should not be used in patients with severe anaemia, closed angle glaucoma, severe hypotension or severe hypovolaemia.
should not be used in patients with marked anaemia, sever hypotension, closed angle glaucoma, toxic pulmonary oedema or hypovolaemia.

items.t: MR tablets: constrictive cardiomyopathy and pericarditis, aortic stenosis, cardiac tamponade, mitral stenosis, severe anaemia.

src.q: Constrictive cardiomyopathy and pericarditis, aortic stenosis, cardiac tamponade, mitral stenosis and severe anaemia.

items.t: Relative contraindications (immediate-release tablets and MR tablets): severe cerebrovascular insufficiency or hypotension.

src.q: Severe cerebrovascular insufficiency or hypotension are relative contraindications to the use of Imdur.

items.t: Use with caution after recent myocardial infarction, and in hypothyroidism, hypothermia, malnutrition, severe liver or renal disease (immediate-release tablets and MR capsules). MR capsules: avoid lowering systolic BP below 90 mmHg.

src.q: should be used with caution in patients who have a recent history of myocardial infarction, or who are suffering from closed-angle glaucoma, hypothyroidism, hypothermia, malnutrition and sever liver or renal disease.
Reducing systolic blood-pressure below 90 mmHg must be avoided.

items.t: Postural hypotension and syncope can occur; circulatory collapse may follow the first dose with labile circulation (immediate-release: also in patients already on ACE inhibitors). Nitrate hypotension may come with paradoxical bradycardia and worse angina.

src.q: Symptoms of circulatory collapse may arise after first dose in patients with labile circulation and in patients already taking ACE inhibitors.
Hypotension induced by nitrates may be accompanied by paradoxical bradycardia and increased angina.

items.t: Tolerance and cross-tolerance to other nitrates can develop if not taken as directed (immediate-release: keep the asymmetric nitrate-low period). Avoid continuously high doses (MR capsules).

src.q: If the tablets are not taken as indicated (see section 4.2) tolerance to the medication and cross-tolerance to other nitrates may occur.
Continuously high dosages should be avoided.

items.t: MR capsules: caution in hypoxaemia and ventilation/perfusion imbalance (lung disease, ischaemic heart failure). Fast gastrointestinal transit may reduce release from MR formulations.

src.q: Caution should be exercised in patients with hypoxaemia and ventilation/perfusion imbalance due to lung disease or ischaemic heart failure.
In patients with decreased gastrointestinal transit time, and using prolonged-release formulation of isosorbide mononitrate, a decrease in release of the active ingredient may occur.

items.t: MR capsules: do not interrupt nitrate therapy in order to take a PDE5 inhibitor (risk of angina attack).

src.q: Elantan therapy should not be interrupted to take phosphodiesterase inhibitor-containing products (e.g. sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil), because the risk of inducing an attack of angina pectoris could increase by doing so

items.t: Immediate-release tablets and MR capsules contain lactose and sucrose: patients with rare hereditary galactose or fructose intolerance, total lactase deficiency, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrase-isomaltase insufficiency should not take them.

src.q: patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose or fructose intolerance, total lactase deficiency, sucrase-isomaltase insufficiency glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take this medicine.
Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take this medicine.
Due to the presence of sucrose, patients with rare hereditary problems of fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrase-isomaltase insufficiency should not take this medicine.

items.t: PDE5 inhibitors (sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil): potentiate hypotension; possible syncope, MI or life-threatening cardiovascular complications. Must not be used together.

src.q: Patients who are on Isosorbide Mononitrate Tablets therapy therefore must not use phosphodiesterase type-5 inhibitors.
Imdur and Phosphodiesterase Type 5 Inhibitors (e.g. sildenafil) must not be given concomitantly.

items.t: Blood-pressure-lowering medicines (beta-blockers, calcium-channel blockers, vasodilators, ARBs, ACE inhibitors), neuroleptics, tricyclic antidepressants and alcohol may increase the hypotensive effect. MR capsules: if the BP fall with ACE inhibitors or arterial vasodilators is excessive, consider reducing one or both doses.

src.q: Concurrent administration of drugs with blood pressure lowering properties, e.g, beta-blockers, calcium channel blockers, vasodilators, alprostadil, aldesleukin, angiotensin II receptor antagonist, ACE inhibitors etc. may potentiate the hypotensive effect

The concurrent intake of ISMN with ACE-inhibitors or arterial vasodilators could be a desirable interaction unless the antihypertensive effects are excessive in which case consider reducing the dose of one or both drugs.

items.t: Riociguat: contraindicated (immediate-release tablets and MR capsules). Dihydroergotamine: levels and hypertensive effect may rise.

src.q: The use of isosorbide mononitrate with riociguat, a stimulator of soluble guanylate cyclase, is contra-indicated
may increase the blood level of dihydroergotamine and its hypertensive effect.

items.t: Immediate-release SmPC: reduce the dose in renal impairment (no threshold given); use with caution in severe renal disease.

src.q: Dosage should be reduced in patients with renal or hepatic impairment.

items.t: MR capsules: use with caution in severe renal disease. MR tablets: special care in older people with marked renal insufficiency. No numeric renal thresholds in any SmPC used.

src.q: Also in patients who are suffering from hypothyroidism, hypothermia, malnutrition, severe liver or severe renal disease.
special care may be needed in those with increased susceptibility to hypotension or marked hepatic or renal insufficiency

items.t: Immediate-release SmPC: reduce the dose in hepatic impairment; caution in severe liver disease.

src.q: Dosage should be reduced in patients with renal or hepatic impairment.

items.t: MR capsules: caution in severe liver disease. MR tablets: special care in older people with marked hepatic insufficiency.

src.q: severe liver or severe renal disease
marked hepatic or renal insufficiency

items.t: Immediate-release tablets and MR tablets: safety and efficacy in pregnancy not established.

src.q: The safety and efficacy of Isosorbide Mononitrate Tablets during pregnancy or lactation has not been established.
The safety and efficacy of Imdur during pregnancy or lactation has not been established.

items.t: MR capsules: no data suggesting harm, but safety not established; use only if the physician judges benefit outweighs possible hazard.

src.q: Isosorbide mononitrate should only be used in pregnancy and during lactation if, in the opinion of the physician, the possible benefits outweigh the possible hazards.

items.t: Immediate-release tablets and MR tablets: safety in lactation not established.

src.q: The safety and efficacy of Isosorbide Mononitrate Tablets during pregnancy or lactation has not been established.

items.t: MR capsules: unknown whether nitrates pass into milk; use caution. No SPS breastfeeding page for nitrates was found.

src.q: It is not known whether nitrates are excreted in human milk and therefore caution should be exercised when administered to nursing women.

items.t: Fertility: no human data (MR capsules).

src.q: There is no data available on the effect of isosorbide mononitrate on fertility in humans.

items.t: Very common: throbbing headache (usually fades after 1-3 weeks). Common: hypotension or light-headedness on standing (especially at start or after a dose increase), dizziness, tachycardia, nausea (MR tablets), somnolence and asthenia (MR capsules).

src.q: A very common (>10% of patients) adverse reaction to Isosorbide Mononitrate Tablets is throbbing headache.
At the start of therapy or when the dosage is increased, hypotension and/or light headedness in the upright position are commonly observed
Nervous system disorders Common Headache, dizziness
Cardiac and vascular disorders Common Hypotension, tachycardia Gastrointestinal disorders Common Nausea
very common: headache, common: dizziness (including dizziness postural), somnolence.

items.t: Uncommon: collapse (sometimes with bradyarrhythmia and syncope); severe hypotension that may worsen angina.

src.q: Uncommonly collapse may occur (sometimes accompanied by bradyarrhythmia and syncope). Uncommonly severe hypotension may lead to enhanced angina symptoms.

items.t: Rare/single cases: exfoliative dermatitis; angioedema (MR capsules, frequency not known). Nitrate-induced pituitary apoplexy reported in undiagnosed pituitary tumours.

src.q: In single cases exfoliative dermatitis may occur.
Immune system disorders: not known: angioedema
Nitrate-induced pituitary apoplexy has been reported in patients with undiagnosed pituitary tumours.

monitoring.note: No laboratory or routine monitoring stated in the SmPCs used; no SPS monitoring page found for nitrates.

items.t: Immediate-release: swallow whole with a drink of water; asymmetric dosing to leave a nitrate-low period.

src.q: It is recommended that the tablets should be swallowed whole with a drink of water.

items.t: MR tablets: do not chew or crush; swallow whole with half a glass of water, in the morning. The empty tablet matrix may be seen in the stool.

src.q: Imdur Tablets must not be chewed or crushed. They should be swallowed whole with half a glass of water.
Very occasionally the matrix may pass through the gastrointestinal tract without disintegrating and be found visible in the stool

items.t: MR capsules: take in the morning.

src.q: One capsule to be taken daily, or two capsules daily, in the morning.

items.t: Never take sildenafil, tadalafil or vardenafil (erectile dysfunction medicines) with this medicine.

src.q: Patients who undergo a maintenance treatment with Elantan should be informed that they must not use phosphodiesterase inhibitor-containing products (e.g. sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil).

items.t: Use a GTN spray or sublingual tablet for an acute angina attack; this medicine does not treat attacks.

src.q: In the event of an acute angina attack, sublingual treatment such as a GTN spray or tablet should be used instead of isosorbide mononitrate tablets.

items.t: Avoid alcohol (severe postural hypotension). Dizziness, tiredness or blurred vision at the start may affect driving.

src.q: Severe postural hypotension with light headedness and dizziness is frequently observed after the consumption of alcohol, therefore alcohol should be avoided during treatment.
Dizziness, tiredness or blurred vision might occur at the start of treatment.

items.t: Headache is common at first and usually settles within 1-3 weeks. Do not stop suddenly.

src.q: The incidence of headache diminishes gradually or disappears after 1-3 weeks

items.t: Short-term use: occasional constipation; bowel regulation in bed-ridden patients; pain-free evacuation with haemorrhoids.

src.q: For short-term use a) in cases of occasional constipation, b) to achieve bowel regulation in bed-ridden patients, c) in cases of haemorrhoids to achieve pain free evacuation.

items.t: Use only if diet change or pure bulk-forming agents fail. Debilitated and/or elderly patients need medical supervision.

src.q: Manevac should only be used if a therapeutic effect cannot be achieved by a change of diet or the administration of pure bulk forming agents.
The treatment of debilitated patients and / or elderly patients requires medical supervision.

items.t: MHRA (stimulant laxatives, including senna): use only if bulk-forming and osmotic laxatives are ineffective.

src.q: stimulant laxatives should only be used if other laxatives (bulk-forming and osmotic) are ineffective

items.t: Adults, elderly and children over 12: 5-10 g (1-2 level spoonfuls or sachets) once daily at night (not immediately before bed-time). Maximum 30 mg hydroxyanthracene glycosides (10 g granules) a day. Use the smallest dose that gives a soft-formed motion.

src.q: One (5g) or two (10g) level measuring spoons to be taken once daily at night.
The maximum daily dose of hydroxyanthracene glycosides is 30 mg.
This product should not be taken immediately prior to bed-time.

items.t: Not for more than 1 week; 2-3 doses in that week are usually enough.

src.q: Not to be used for more than 1 week (see section 4.4). Usually it is sufficient to take this medicinal product up to two to three times during that week.

items.t: Contraindicated under 12 years.

src.q: Use in children below the age of 12 years is contraindicated (see section 4.3)

items.t: Hypersensitivity to the active substances or excipients; children under 12; pregnancy and lactation.

src.q: Hypersensitivity to the active substances or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1. Children under 12 years of age. Pregnancy and lactation

items.t: Sudden change in bowel habit persisting over 2 weeks; undiagnosed rectal bleeding; failure to defecate after a laxative.

src.q: Patients with a sudden change in bowel habit that persists for more than 2 weeks Undiagnosed rectal bleeding and failure to defecate following the use of a laxative.

items.t: Possible or existing ileus, intestinal atony, GI stenosis, oesophageal/cardia disease, paralysis of the intestine or megacolon.

src.q: possible or existing bowel obstruction (ileus) intestinal atony abnormal narrowing (stenosis) of the gastrointestinal tract diseases of the oesophagus and cardia paralysis of the intestine or megacolon

items.t: Acute inflammatory bowel disease (e.g. Crohn's, ulcerative colitis, appendicitis), severe dehydration, abdominal pain of unknown origin, dysphagia.

src.q: acute inflammatory bowel disease (e.g. Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, appendicitis) severe dehydration (with loss of fluid and electrolytes) abdominal pain of unknown origin dysphagia

items.t: Always take with enough liquid: with too little fluid, bulk-forming agents can cause throat/oesophageal obstruction with choking, and intestinal obstruction.

src.q: When taken with inadequate fluid amounts, bulk forming agents can cause obstruction of the throat and oesophagus with choking and intestinal obstruction.

items.t: With medicines that inhibit peristalsis (e.g. opioids): use only under medical supervision (risk of ileus).

src.q: In order to decrease the risk of gastrointestinal obstruction (ileus) Manevac should be used together with medicinal products known to inhibit peristaltic movement (e.g. opioids,) only under medical supervision.

items.t: Patients on cardiac glycosides, antiarrhythmics, QT-prolonging medicines, diuretics, corticosteroids or liquorice root must consult a doctor first.

src.q: Patients taking cardiac glycosides, antiarrhythmic medicinal products, medicinal products inducing QT-prolongation, diuretics, adrenocorticosteroids or liquorice root, have to consult a doctor before taking Manevac concomitantly.

items.t: Avoid long-term use (over 1 week): laxative dependence, atonic colon, fluid/electrolyte imbalance and hypokalaemia. Stop and seek advice if no effect within 3 days or abdominal pain.

src.q: Long-term use of laxatives (more than 1 week) should be avoided.
Prolonged and excessive use may lead to fluid and electrolyte imbalance and hypokalaemia.
If the constipation does not resolve within 3 days or if abdominal pain occurs or in cases of any irregularity of faeces, the use of Manevac should be discontinued and medical advice must be sought.

items.t: Contains potent allergens: hypersensitivity can follow oral use or skin contact.

src.q: Manevac contains potent allergens. As a consequence after oral administration or contact with the skin, Manevac may cause hypersensitivity reactions

items.t: Sucrose: fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrase-isomaltase insufficiency should not take.

src.q: Patients with rare hereditary problems of fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrase-isomaltase insufficiency should not take this medicine.

items.t: May delay absorption of minerals, vitamin B12, cardiac glycosides, coumarins, carbamazepine and lithium: separate from other medicines by ½ to 1 hour.

src.q: Enteral absorption of concomitantly administered medicines such as minerals, vitamins (B12), cardiac glycosides, coumarin derivatives, carbamazepine and lithium may be delayed.
For this reason Manevac should not be taken ½ to 1 hour before or after intake of other medicinal products.

items.t: Antidiabetic therapy may need adjustment (medical supervision); insulin dose may need reducing if taken with meals.

src.q: Diabetic patients should take Manevac only under medical supervision because adjustment of anti-diabetic therapy may be necessary.
If Manevac is taken together with meals by insulin dependent diabetic patients it may be necessary to reduce the insulin dose.

items.t: Thyroid hormones: medical supervision; dose may need adjusting.

src.q: Use of Manevac concomitantly with thyroid hormones requires medical supervision because the dose of the thyroid hormones may have to be adjusted.

items.t: Laxative-induced hypokalaemia: interacts with cardiac glycosides, antiarrhythmics and QT-prolonging medicines; diuretics and corticosteroids may enhance electrolyte imbalance.

src.q: Hypokalaemia (resulting from long-term laxative abuse) potentiates the action of cardiac glycosides and interacts with antiarrhythmic medicinal products
Concomitant use with other medicinal products inducing hypokalaemia (e.g. diuretics, adrenocorticosteroids and liquorice root) may enhance electrolyte imbalance.

items.t: Kidney disorders: possible electrolyte imbalance. With fluid loss where dehydration may be harmful (e.g. renal insufficiency), stop and restart only under medical supervision.

src.q: Patients with kidney disorders should be aware of possible electrolyte imbalance.

In patients suffering from fluid loss where dehydration may be harmful (e.g. renal insufficiency, elderly patients) use of the product should be discontinued and only be restarted under medical supervision.

items.t: No hepatic dosing advice. Chronic overdose of anthranoid-containing medicines may cause toxic hepatitis.

src.q: Chronic ingested overdoses of anthranoid containing medicinal products may lead to toxic hepatitis.

items.t: SmPC: contraindicated in pregnancy (genotoxicity data for some senna anthranoids).

src.q: The use during pregnancy is contraindicated because of experimental data concerning a genotoxic risk of several anthranoids in Senna

items.t: BUMPS (differs from the SmPC): bulk-forming laxatives such as ispaghula are often tried first and are safe in pregnancy; stimulant laxatives such as senna are tried only when others have not helped.

src.q: are often tried first and are safe in pregnancy.
Stimulant laxatives only tend to be tried when those above have not helped.

items.t: SmPC: contraindicated during lactation (rhein passes into milk in small amounts).

src.q: The use during lactation is contraindicated because after administration of anthranoids, active metabolites, such as rhein, were excreted in breast milk in small amounts.

items.t: SPS (differs from the SmPC): ispaghula husk and standardised senna can each be used during breastfeeding.

src.q: Ispaghula husk can be used during breastfeeding.
Standardised senna preparations can be used during breastfeeding.

reproductive.note: UK SmPC: fertility studies not performed.

items.t: Flatulence (usually settles); abdominal pain, spasm and liquid stools (especially irritable colon; reduce dose); harmless yellow or red-brown urine. Frequencies not known.

src.q: Flatulence may occur with the use of Manevac, this generally disappears in the course of the treatment.
Yellow or red-brown (pH dependent) discolouration of urine by metabolites, which is not clinically significant, may occur during the treatment.

items.t: Oesophageal or intestinal obstruction and faecal impaction, especially if swallowed with too little fluid.

src.q: Abdominal distension and risk of intestinal or oesophageal obstruction (e.g. dysphagia) and faecal impaction may occur, particularly if swallowed with insufficient fluid.

items.t: Hypersensitivity: rhinitis, conjunctivitis, bronchospasm and sometimes anaphylaxis.

src.q: hypersensitivity reactions such as rhinitis, conjunctivitis, bronchospasm and in some cases anaphylaxis

items.t: No result within 3 days, abdominal pain or irregular stools: stop and seek medical advice.

src.q: If the constipation does not resolve within 3 days or if abdominal pain occurs or in cases of any irregularity of faeces, the use of Manevac should be discontinued and medical advice must be sought.

items.t: Sit upright. Place the granules dry on the tongue and swallow without chewing with a glass of water or other liquid; keep up fluid intake.

src.q: The patient should be sitting in an upright position prior to administration of the granules.
should be placed dry on the tongue and, without chewing or crushing, swallowed with a glass of water

items.t: Keep ½ to 1 hour between this and other medicines.

src.q: An interval of half an hour to one hour should be kept after taking another medicinal product.

items.t: Always take with plenty of liquid; stop and seek help if chest pain, vomiting, or difficulty swallowing or breathing.

src.q: Symptoms can be chest pain, vomiting, or difficulty in swallowing or breathing.

items.t: Do not take immediately before going to bed.

src.q: This product should not be taken immediately prior to bed-time.

items.t: Adults and adolescents: start 15-45 ml daily, maintenance 15-30 ml daily, as a single dose or two divided doses. Adjust after a few days to response; effect may take 2-3 days.

src.q: Adults and adolescents 15-45 ml, corresponding to 1-3 sachets 15-30 ml, corresponding to 1-2 sachets
Lactulose may be given as a single daily dose or in two divided doses.
Several days (2-3 days) of treatment may be needed before treatment effect occurs.

items.t: Adults: start 30-45 ml three to four times daily; adjust to a maintenance dose giving two or three soft stools each day.

src.q: Starting dose : 3 to 4 times daily 30-45 ml (6-9 x 5 ml spoonfuls) or 2-3 sachets.
This dose may be adjusted to the maintenance dose to achieve two or three soft stools each day.

items.t: Elderly, renal or hepatic impairment: no special dose recommendations (negligible systemic exposure).

src.q: Elderly patients and patients with renal or hepatic insufficiency No special dosage recommendations exist, since systemic exposure to lactulose is negligible.

items.t: Constipation: children 7-14 years start 15 ml daily, maintenance 10-15 ml daily; 1-6 years 5-10 ml daily; infants under 1 year up to 5 ml daily.

src.q: Children (7-14 years) 15 ml, corresponding to 1 sachet 10-15 ml, corresponding to 1 sachet*
Children (1-6 years) 5-10 ml 5-10 ml Infants under 1 year up to 5 ml up to 5 ml

items.t: Laxatives in children should be exceptional and under medical supervision.

src.q: Use of laxatives in children should be exceptional and under medical supervision.

items.t: Hepatic encephalopathy: safety and efficacy not established in children (newborn to 18 years).

src.q: The safety and efficacy in children (newborn to 18 years of age) with HE have not been established.

src.q: Painful abdominal symptoms of undetermined cause should be evaluated to exclude undiagnosed perforation or obstruction

items.t: Chronic use of unadjusted doses and misuse can cause diarrhoea and electrolyte disturbance.

src.q: Chronic use of unadjusted doses and misuse can lead to diarrhoea and disturbance of the electrolyte balance.

items.t: Diabetes: constipation doses should not be a problem; the higher HE doses may need to be taken into account.

src.q: The dose normally used in constipation should not pose a problem for diabetics.
The dose used in the treatment of HE is usually much higher and may need to be taken into consideration for diabetics.

items.t: Rare hereditary galactose or fructose intolerance, total lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption: should not take. Lactose intolerance: give with care.

src.q: patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose or fructose intolerance, the total lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take this medicine.
